title: Silver usage grain: defensive casts + healthstone/potion usage events
description:
## Why

`silver.defensive_buff_window` captures aura windows but cannot answer "what was used": healthstone/potion usage isn't captured at all, and cast events are the ground truth needed for cooldown inference. Aura windows alone also miss instant/absorb-style usages.

## Acceptance criteria

* New silver projection (e.g. `silver.survival_action`) with one row per defensive/healthstone/potion use per player per encounter: timestamp ms into fight, cast spell ID, kind/category, and heal amount + overheal for consumable heals (join `SPELL_CAST_SUCCESS` with the resulting `SPELL_HEAL`).
* Gated by the game-data catalog — this must not become a generic cast warehouse (silver layer boundary rule).
* Rebuildable per encounter like other silver projections, keyed on `encounter_dim_id`.
* Tests cover a real-log fixture containing at least one healthstone or potion use and one defensive cast; current-tier potion spell IDs are resolved from observed real-log events, not memory.

Depends on the retail-current catalog ticket. Initiative: `docs/initiatives/07-defensives-and-consumables.md`.

title: Retail-current defensive & consumable catalog with cooldown/talent metadata
description:
## Why

The raid lead's #1 question set for the deployed mirror is "Defensives. And rocks/pots." The existing `WeGoNext.GameData.DefensiveBuffs` catalog is aura-IDs only — no cast IDs, no cooldown durations, no class/spec/talent mapping, no healthstones/potions — and is unverified against current retail (Midnight 12.x). Availability inference ("was it on cooldown when they died?") needs cooldown/charge metadata; "what was talented" needs talent association.

## Acceptance criteria

* Game-data catalog covers personal defensives per class/spec for **current retail**, plus Healthstone and current-tier health potions. Each entry carries: cast spell ID, aura spell ID(s), base cooldown, charges where relevant, category (personal/external/immunity/consumable), and talent association where the ability is talent-gated.
* Spell IDs are verified against observed events in imported retail logs (or retail-only references) — **no MoP-Classic/Classic/other-flavor IDs**. DBM ships multi-flavor mods; do not source IDs from them blindly. Where an ID cannot be confirmed, it stays out rather than guessed in.
* Consumables model the shared potion cooldown and per-combat usage constraints so availability inference is possible downstream.
* Catalog stays plain data tables gating silver projection (same pattern as `DefensiveBuffs` today); existing duplicate/suspect entries (e.g. double Fortifying Brew IDs, Mirror Image) are audited.

Initiative: `docs/initiatives/07-defensives-and-consumables.md`.

title: Death-window survival analysis: died-through / available-but-unused / on-cooldown
description:
## Why

The coaching question at every death: did they use anything, did they die *through* a pot or defensive (used it and died anyway), and what was sitting available — including rocks/pots?

## Acceptance criteria

* For each `silver.death`, a derived read model (gold/document-section input) reporting:
  * survival actions used within the death window (configurable, default ~10s before death),
  * actions active at the moment of death → "died through X",
  * catalog defensives that were talented and off cooldown at death → "available but unused",
  * healthstone/potion availability at death (shared potion cooldown state, healthstone usage).
* Cooldown availability is inferred (last use + base cooldown; encounter-start state unknown) and the read model labels it as inference (e.g. "likely available"), not asserted fact.
* Tests against real or fixture deaths covering at least: one "died with defensive available" case and one "died through a pot/defensive" case.

Depends on the silver usage grain and talent loadout tickets. Initiative: `docs/initiatives/07-defensives-and-consumables.md`.

title: Document store seam: FileSystem + R2 adapters
description:
> **Reworked 2026-07-06** for the JSON-first encounter-document architecture — see `docs/ENCOUNTER_DOCUMENTS_DESIGN.md`.

## Why

Documents need one read/write seam with two homes: local disk (parser mode) and a private Cloudflare R2 bucket (upload target and public read source). Code stays S3-generic so the provider is swappable.

## Acceptance criteria

* `WeGoNext.Documents.Store` behaviour (`put/2`, `fetch/1`, `exists?/1`; no delete in v1) with two adapters: `Store.FileSystem` rooted at config `:documents_root` (env `DOCUMENTS_ROOT`, default a git-ignored `we_go_next/documents/`), and `Store.R2` via `Req` + the `req_s3` plugin (SigV4), env-driven endpoint/bucket/credentials.

* Public mode reads with R2 **read** credentials from Gigalixir env.
* FileSystem adapter unit tests; R2 adapter tested against a `Req.Test` stub; a manual real-bucket smoke is documented.
